title: Justinian consensual sale constructor with pre-delivery risk and exchange rival
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. Institutes III.22-23 gives a finite bilateral sale state: fixed price creates the contract before delivery, accidental risk can shift to the buyer while title/action rights remain with the vendor, and exchange is distinguished from sale. Writing, earnest, third-party price, condition, and safe-keeping branches alter later states.

source.source_span: complete consensual-contract and purchase/sale sections, especially clauses corresponding to the accessed page's lines 347-369
source.source_limit: public translation; no claim about a specific medieval legal witness or target Vorlage

steps: AGREE(buyer,vendor,object,fixed_price) creates a bilateral consensual sale
A written-formalities gate permits withdrawal before completion; earnest changes withdrawal consequence
A third-party price either closes sale with payment+delivery or leaves it void
After price agreement, accidental risk belongs to buyer before delivery; vendor may retain title/action rights and an express custody promise can reverse the loss assignment
Conditional sale waits for its future condition; object status/fraud changes remedy
Object-for-object exchange remains a distinct contract rather than an arbitrary sale direction

consequence: PRICE_AGREED + NOT_DELIVERED can yield RISK=BUYER while TITLE=VENDOR; explicit safe custody yields RISK=VENDOR for the covered loss. Later delivery closes the remaining title/action relation.

rivals.R-S: Delivery perfects the sale and vendor bears accidental loss before delivery.
rivals.R-X: Every exchange is collapsed into a sale with an arbitrary buyer/price direction.

missing_target_binding: No target word is assigned to consent, price, delivery, risk, title, exchange, or legal action.
likely_failure: Without an independently bound target relation for price/consent/delivery/risk, the state machine is untestable and must not receive invented field assignments.
